cards.text: Jesus has just bowed His head and yielded up His spirit on the cross (John 19:30). It's the day of Preparation, and the next day is a High Sabbath. The Jews go to Pilate, the Roman governor, and ask him to have the legs of the crucified men broken and the bodies removed.

cards.question: The Jews ask Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed. Why?

answers.text: So the bodies won't stay up on the Sabbath
So the soldiers can leave before dark
So the crowd will stop gathering there

cards.question: The soldiers break the legs of only one of the two men crucified with Jesus.

cards.text: Two men, two sets of broken legs. Then the soldiers come to Jesus.

cards.question: When the soldiers reach Jesus, do they break His legs too?

answers.text: No because He is already dead
Yes just like the other two men

cards.text: Instead, one of the soldiers pierces Jesus' side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flow out. I think this one hurts just to read.
The writer hits PAUSE on the story right here. “The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true.”

cards.question: The one who saw the blood and water knows he's telling the truth. Why is he telling it?

answers.text: So readers will blame the soldier

cards.text: Then the writer turns to the Scriptures. The first one he gives says, “Not one of His bones will be broken.”

cards.question: The writer says what the soldiers did at the cross happened so the Scripture would be fulfilled.
The writer adds a second Scripture, from the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 12:10), about the One who was pierced. What does it say people will do?

cards.text: Afterward, a man named Joseph of Arimathea steps forward. He's a disciple of Jesus, but he's been keeping it a secret.

cards.question: Joseph of Arimathea has kept it secret that he's a disciple of Jesus because he fears the ___.

cards.text: Now Joseph goes to Pilate and asks to remove the body of Jesus. I bet that took some nerve after all that hiding.

cards.question: Pilate refuses to let Joseph of Arimathea remove the body of Jesus.

cards.text: Joseph isn't alone. Nicodemus comes too, a Pharisee who had come to Jesus at night (John 3:1-2), and he brings a mixture of myrrh and aloes.

cards.question: Nicodemus brings myrrh and aloes for the body of Jesus. What do he and Joseph use the spices for?

answers.text: To wrap the body for burial
To pay the soldiers at the cross
To burn as an offering at the temple

cards.text: And Nicodemus's mixture weighs about SEVENTY-FIVE POUNDS. The two men take the body of Jesus and wrap it in linen cloths with the spices.

cards.question: Joseph and Nicodemus follow the Jewish burial custom when they wrap the body of Jesus.

cards.text: Now, in the place where Jesus was crucified, there's a garden.

cards.question: What is in the garden near where Jesus was crucified?

answers.text: A new tomb where no one had been laid
The tomb where Lazarus had been buried
The pool where a lame man had waited

cards.question: Why do Joseph and Nicodemus lay Jesus in the new tomb in the garden?

answers.text: It is the day of Preparation and the tomb is nearby
Jesus had asked to be buried in that garden
Pilate had ordered that He be buried there

cards.text: With the day of Preparation on them and the tomb close by, they lay Jesus there. Hold that thought, friend, because this story still has more to tell.
